The [[1928 Winter Olympics]], officially known as the II Olympic Winter Games and commonly known as St. Moritz 1928, were an international multi-sport event held in [[St. Moritz]], Switzerland, from 11 to 19 February 1928. A total of 464 athletes representing 25 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) participated, which included 9 NOCs more than the [[1924 Winter Olympics|inaugural Winter Games]] held four years earlier in [[Chamonix]], France. The 9 NOCs were all first time entrants at the Winter Games: [[Argentina at the 1928 Winter Olympics|Argentina]], [[Estonia at the 1928 Winter Olympics|Estonia]], [[Germany at the 1928 Winter Olympics|Germany]], [[Japan at the 1928 Winter Olympics|Japan]], [[Lithuania at the 1928 Winter Olympics|Lithuania]], [[Luxembourg at the 1928 Winter Olympics|Luxembourg]], [[Mexico at the 1928 Winter Olympics|Mexico]], the [[Netherlands at the 1928 Winter Olympics|Netherlands]], and [[Romania at the 1928 Winter Olympics|Romania]].<ref name=first>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/the-first-true-olympic-winter-games |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816052151/https://www.olympics.com/en/news/the-first-true-olympic-winter-games |archive-date=16 August 2024 |access-date=14 February 2025 |title=The first true Olympic Winter Games |work=[[International Olympic Committee]] |url-status=live }}</ref> The games featured 14 events in 4 [[Winter Olympic sports|sports]] in 8 disciplines, with [[Skeleton at the 1928 Winter Olympics|skeleton]] making its debut appearance.<ref name=factbook>{{cite web|url=https://stillmed.olympics.com/media/Documents/Olympic-Games/Factsheets/The-Olympic-Winter-Games.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130171949/https://stillmed.olympics.com/media/Documents/Olympic-Games/Factsheets/The-Olympic-Winter-Games.pdf |archive-date=30 November 2022 |date=14 October 2021 |page=1 |title=Factsheet: The Winter Olympic Games |work=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=14 February 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/sports/SKN |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250214145922/https://www.olympedia.org/sports/SKN |title=Skeleton |archive-date=14 February 2025 |access-date=1 March 2025 |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live }}</ref> These games were the first Winter Games to be held as a stand-alone event, not in conjunction with a Summer Olympics.<ref name=first /> It also replaced the [[Nordic Games]], a former international multi-sport event that also focused primarily on [[winter sports]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://isoh.org/wp-content/uploads/JOH-Archives/JOHv2n2h.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250211075306/https://isoh.org/wp-content/uploads/JOH-Archives/JOHv2n2h.pdf |archive-date=11 February 2025 |access-date=14 February 2025 |date=1994 |publisher=[[International Society of Olympic Historians]] |journal=Journal of Olympic History |version=2 |last1=Edgeworth |first1=Ron |pages=34–35 |title=The Nordic Games and the Origins of the Winter Olympic Games }}</ref>

Overall, athletes representing 12 NOCs won at least one medal, and 6 NOCs won at least one gold medal. [[Norway at the 1928 Winter Olympics|Norway]] won the most gold medals and the most overall medals, with 6 and 15 respectively.<ref name=medaltable /> [[France at the 1928 Winter Olympics|France]]'s team won their first Winter Olympic gold medal, with figure skaters [[Andrée Joly]] and [[Pierre Brunet (figure skater)|Pierre Brunet]] winning gold in the [[Figure skating at the 1928 Winter Olympics – Pairs|pair skating event]].<ref>{{cite book|isbn=978-0810868595 |title=Historical Dictionary of Figure Skating |last1=Hines |first1=James R. |page=45 |date=22 April 2011 }}</ref> Germany's and [[Czechoslovakia at the 1928 Winter Olympics|Czechoslovakia]]'s teams obtained their first Winter Olympic medals, with the former winning bronze in the [[Bobsleigh at the 1928 Winter Olympics|five-man bobsleigh event]] from bobsledders [[Hans Hess (bobsleigh)|Hans Heß]], [[Sebastian Huber]], [[Hanns Kilian]], [[Valentin Krempl]], and [[Hanns Nägle]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/236 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126131032/https://www.olympedia.org/results/236 |archive-date=26 January 2025 |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live |title=Four/Five, Men }}</ref> and the latter also winning bronze but in the [[Ski jumping at the 1928 Winter Olympics|men's individual ski jumping event]] from [[Rudolf Burkert]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympijskytym.cz/en/athlete/rudolf-burkert |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241213171553/https://www.olympijskytym.cz/en/athlete/rudolf-burkert |archive-date=13 December 2024 |title=Rudolph Burkert |lang=cs |work=[[Czech Olympic Committee]] |url-status=live }}</ref>

Skier [[Johan Grøttumsbraaten]] of Norway and speed skater [[Clas Thunberg]] of [[Finland at the 1928 Winter Olympics|Finland]] tied for the most gold medals won by an individual at the games, with two each. Speed skater [[Bernt Evensen]] of Norway won the most overall medals for an individual at the games, winning three medals with one gold, one silver, and one bronze.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/30/medal |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240826084626/https://www.olympedia.org/editions/30/medal |archive-date=26 August 2024 |title=Medal winners Sankt Moritz 1928 |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live |access-date=14 February 2025 }}</ref>

Sweden and Norway achieved [[podium sweep]]s at the games, with the latter achieving two. The former swept the [[Cross-country skiing at the 1928 Winter Olympics – Men's 50 kilometre|men's 50 kilometre event in cross-country skiing]] with [[Per-Erik Hedlund]] winning the gold, [[Gustaf Jonsson]] winning the silver, and [[Volger Andersson]] winning the bronze.<ref name=protest>{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-evening-journal-protest-cancellation/165453532/ |date=14 February 1928 |work=[[The Evening Journal]] |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=14 February 2025 |title=Protest Cancellation of Olympic Ice Race with America on Top |agency=[[Associated Press]] |page=14 }}</ref> The latter swept the [[Cross-country skiing at the 1928 Winter Olympics – Men's 18 kilometre|men's 18 kilometre event in cross-country skiing]] with Grøttumsbråten winning the gold, [[Ole Hegge]] winning the silver, and [[Reidar Ødegaard]] winning the bronze,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-toronto-star-winter-olympic-cross-co/165205835/ |work=[[Toronto Star]] |title=Winter Olympic Cross-country Sweeps |date=24 February 2014 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |page=49 |access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref> and the [[Nordic combined at the 1928 Winter Olympics|individual Nordic combined event]] with Grøttumsbråten again winning the gold, [[Hans Vinjarengen]] winning the silver, and [[Jon Snersrud]] winning the bronze.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/st-moritz-1928/results/nordic-combined |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241001134100/https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/st-moritz-1928/results/nordic-combined |archive-date=1 October 2024 |title=St. Moritz 1928 Nordic Combined Results |work=[[International Olympic Committee]] |url-status=live |access-date=14 February 2025 }}</ref>

==Medals==
{{see also|Olympic medal}}
[[File:Rudolf Burkert 1928.jpg|[[Rudolf Burkert]] won the first Winter Olympic medal for Czechoslovakia, winning bronze in the men's individual ski jumping event.|thumb |alt=Rudolf Bukert from the torso up wearing a sweater. Image is in black and white.]]

The medals used for the 1928 Winter Olympics were minted by Huguenin Frères in [[Le Locle]] and were designed by Arnold Hünerwadel. The [[obverse]] of the medals featured a design of a female figure skater surrounded with [[snowflake]]s. The reverse of the medals featured the [[Olympic rings]], the official name of the games and the host city in French, and an [[olive branch]] on the left- and right-hand sides.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/st-moritz-1928/medal-design |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240911065006/https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/st-moritz-1928/medal-design |archive-date=11 September 2024 |access-date=1 February 2025 |title=St. Moritz 1928 Olympic Medals - Design, History & Photos |work=[[International Olympic Committee]] |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Medal table==
The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |website=[[The Independent]] | date=11 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |access-date=12 August 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |website=[[The New York Times]] | date=18 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite web |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |website=[[Diario AS]] | date=10 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |access-date=11 August 2024 |language=en-us}}</ref>

In speed skating, two gold medals and three bronze medals with no silver medal were awarded in the [[Speed skating at the 1928 Winter Olympics – Men's 500 metres|men's 500 metres event]] after a tie for first place and a three-way tie for third place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/st-moritz-1928/results/speed-skating/500m-men |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241009092344/https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/st-moritz-1928/results/speed-skating/500m-men |archive-date=9 October 2024 |url-status=live |access-date=13 February 2025 |work=[[International Olympic Committee]] |title=St. Moritz 1928 Speed skating 500m men Results }}</ref> The [[Speed skating at the 1928 Winter Olympics – Men's 10,000 metres|men's 10,000 metres event]] resulted in having no medals being awarded after the finals were cancelled by a referee due to thawing ice. [[Irving Jaffee]] of the [[United States at the 1928 Winter Olympics|United States]] was briefly credited as the champion of the event by the IOC but the decision was overruled by the [[International Skating Union]] (ISU) and the ruling that there would be no medalists was restored. The [[United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee|United States NOC]] submitted a protest to the decision by the ISU but it was rejected as they had submitted it too late.<ref name=protest /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/964 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250114124805/https://www.olympedia.org/results/964 |archive-date=14 January 2025 |title=10,000 metres, Men |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live |access-date=14 February 2025 }}</ref>
